chunks: And from him, from Ahmad ibn Muhammad, from Ali ibn Hadid, from Jamil ibn Darraj, from Zurara, who said:

Abu Ja'far (peace be upon him) commanded Abu Abd Allah (peace be upon him), so he made me read a scroll of the obligatory shares (of inheritance), and I saw that most of what was in it was based on four shares.

key_terms.أَسْهُمٍ: Shares or portions into which an estate is divided for inheritance distribution among heirs
key_terms.الْفَرَائِضِ: The obligatory prescribed shares of inheritance as specified in the Quran and elaborated in hadith literature
key_terms.جُلَّ: Most, the greater part — indicating the predominant but not exclusive pattern observed in the inheritance document
key_terms.صَحِيفَةَ الْفَرَائِضِ: A written scroll or document containing the rules of the obligatory shares of inheritance (fara'id), a foundational text in Islamic succession law

ai.seo_question: What does the hadith of Zurara say about Imam al-Baqir's scroll on inheritance shares in Al-Kafi?
ai.summary: This hadith reports that Imam al-Baqir (AS) instructed his son Imam al-Sadiq (AS) to show Zurara, one of their most trusted companions, a written document detailing the rules of Islamic inheritance (fara'id). Zurara observes that the majority of the cases documented in the scroll were calculated on the basis of four shares. This narration is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it preserves a direct transmission of inheritance law from the Imams through their authoritative written records.

en.hubeali: And from him, from Ahmad Bin Muhammad, from Ali Bin Hadeed, from Jameel Bin Darraj, from Zurara who said,

‘Abu Ja’far<sup>asws</sup> instructed Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> so he<sup>asws</sup> made me read a parchment of the Obligatory (legislated shares of inheritances). So I saw most of what was therein were upon four shares’.
en.sarwar: 4. It is narrated from the narrator of the previous Hadith from Ahmad ibn Muhammad from Ali ibn Fladid from Jamil ibn Darraj from Zurarah who has narrated the following:
“Abu Ja‘far, commanded abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhim al-Salam, to make me read the booklet on ordained shares and I saw most of them were up to four shares.’”
